comment_count_note: USPS directs comments to PCFederalRegister@usps.gov; automated public comment-count analysis is not available for this item.
title: Ballot Mail for Federal Elections
pass_4_primary_concern: USPS proposes to make outbound federal ballot-mail acceptance depend on voter-linked barcode list infrastructure without providing enough authority, privacy, cost, reliability, and contingency analysis.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The proposal affects federal ballot mail, voter-linked ballot-mail metadata, and operational conditions for mailing ballots in federal elections.
pass_5_red_flag_gates: Harm Before Review Plus Structural Lever
Rights or Sovereignty Burden Without Substantiated Need
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal turns mail visibility and barcode tools into a voter-linked data and acceptance-gateway system without enough authority, privacy, implementation, or reliability support.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Outbound ballot mail could be delayed or refused because of portal, list, barcode, or certification errors before election officials or voters have practical remedies.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule relies on postal mail authority to create a voter-linked ballot-mail data system whose stated purpose includes election-law enforcement.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The proposed standards can provide information regarding the sending of ballots through the mails that would be available for use by law enforcement.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to identify the specific authority for each voter-linked data element and acceptance consequence.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal says states remain responsible for voter eligibility, but federal postal acceptance rules may practically affect state ballot distribution.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Mailings that do not comply with 24.5.1 and 24.5.2 will not be accepted and will be returned.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to explain how acceptance rejection interacts with state election deadlines and lawful emergency or replacement ballot procedures.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: States and local mailers would bear consequences for list or portal errors, while key USPS system specifications and review timelines are not yet in the record.

evidence.quote_or_absence: USPS intends to provide further technical instructions after or alongside finalization.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Request service-level commitments, audit logs, and USPS accountability for portal outages or acceptance-review delays.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal includes state certification and USPS review, but the review design is not detailed enough to evaluate independence or error handling.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for clear validation standards and independent error-resolution procedures.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule would impose data, certification, and verification gates before outbound ballot mail is accepted, placing procedural constraints before ballot distribution.

evidence.quote_or_absence: USPS will review mailings identified as Outbound Federal Ballot Mail prior to acceptance.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to adopt emergency bypasses and post-hoc reconciliation instead of pre-acceptance rejection for time-sensitive ballot mail.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The record asserts law-enforcement and fraud-detection value but does not provide evidence sufficient to justify voter-level barcode association and centralized lists.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The available record does not provide empirical evidence of fraud risk, scan completeness, false-positive rates, or expected enforcement value.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to quantify expected benefits and explain why aggregate or less intrusive reporting would not suffice.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The remedy is a broad ballot-mail acceptance and data system, while the rationale is a general concern about election integrity and mail visibility.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The Executive Order rationale is general, while the proposed DMM text requires names, addresses, outbound IMbs, and return IMbs.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to connect each requirement to a specific operational problem and evaluate narrower remedies.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal assumes diverse election offices and vendors can implement a new federal portal, barcode, certification, and acceptance workflow without a visible implementation plan.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Ballot Portal Users must provide information through the Postal Service Federal Ballot Mail Portal.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for pilots, phased dates, technical support commitments, and documented readiness testing.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposed Federal Ballot Mail Portal is central to compliance, but its specifications, outage handling, permissions, validation, and audit features are not included.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The notice says further technical instructions for entry of data into the proposed portal will be provided later.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to publish portal specifications and reopen comment if those specifications materially affect compliance.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The NPRM invokes fraud risk and federal-law enforcement without defining the specific threat model, baseline rate, or causal link to the selected controls.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The notice refers generally to reducing the risk of fraud and protecting election integrity.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to identify the specific fraud or compliance risks the rule is designed to detect or prevent.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The notice says the rule does not alter voter eligibility, but does not fully account for ballot-mail delay, rejection, or administrative burden effects.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The Postal Service does not purport to alter the eligibility of any individual to vote under state or federal law.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to analyze access and timing impacts even if eligibility rules remain formally unchanged.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal creates voter-linked outbound and return ballot-mail metadata that could be misused or overinterpreted without clear limits.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Required fields include voter name, address, outbound barcode, and return barcode.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for retention limits, access restrictions, audit requirements, and limits on secondary law-enforcement uses.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Core safeguards are deferred: the SORN, technical specifications, correction procedures, and emergency exceptions are not in the NPRM.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Notice regarding the new SORN is forthcoming.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to publish safeguards before finalization or reopen comment after the SORN and technical instructions are available.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule shifts operational burdens and deadline risks to election officials and authorized mailers without quantifying those burdens.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Authorized ballot mailers are responsible for barcode creation under 24.3.1 and 24.3.2 as well as envelope design and printing.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to quantify costs and identify funding, technical assistance, and burden-reduction measures.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal uses list and scan comparisons to flag potential issues for law enforcement, but does not address false positives or lawful reasons for discrepancies.

evidence.quote_or_absence: USPS says the lists allow law enforcement officials to compare mailed and received ballots to detect potential issues meriting further investigation.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to define discrepancy categories, false-positive safeguards, and rules against treating data mismatches as wrongdoing without context.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The record does not describe auditability, data correction, access logs, or public reporting for a system that may affect ballot-mail acceptance.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The available record does not describe audit logs, correction rights, retention periods, access controls, or public performance reporting.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to publish audit and accountability controls as part of the final rule record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: If a mailing is rejected near a deadline, the harm from delayed outbound ballots may occur before further review can meaningfully fix it.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The authorized ballot mailer or Ballot Portal User must address the error(s) before resubmitting the mailing.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for immediate escalation, provisional acceptance, and post-hoc reconciliation for time-sensitive election mail.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal creates a USPS-controlled procedural gateway for outbound federal ballot mail through portal enrollment, certification, list matching, and acceptance verification.

evidence.quote_or_absence: USPS will review mailings prior to acceptance to evaluate whether the mailing meets standards and is being sent to enrolled individuals.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to justify pre-acceptance gatekeeping and compare less disruptive post-acceptance or post-hoc audit models.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule does not clearly distinguish technical noncompliance, suspected fraud, lawful ballot replacement, and administrative mismatch consequences.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Mailings that do not comply will not be accepted and will be returned, but the notice does not specify consequence categories for different error types.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to define error classes, cure procedures, and law-enforcement referral thresholds.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: Key technical standards are forthcoming, so future nonpublic or late-published requirements may control access to ballot-mail acceptance.

evidence.quote_or_absence: USPS intends to provide further technical instructions regarding barcode creation, service type identifiers, acceptance processes, file preparation, documentation submission, and entry of data.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to place all gatekeeping standards in the rule or incorporated public specifications subject to comment.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The structure is coherent as a control system but poorly balanced: high-stakes pre-acceptance consequences are paired with deferred safeguards and limited evidence.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The proposal couples voter-level data collection, acceptance refusal, and law-enforcement rationale without sufficient safeguards or evidence.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask USPS to restructure the rule around visibility, assistance, and reconciliation rather than rejection unless and until safeguards are proven.

conversion_surface.source_surface: Election-mail visibility and mailpiece preparation practices
conversion_surface.converted_surface: Federal ballot-mail acceptance gateway and voter-linked barcode data system
conversion_surface.authority_used: 39 U.S.C. 401 and 404 plus Executive Order 14399 election-integrity rationale
conversion_surface.new_control_point: USPS pre-acceptance verification against Federal Ballot Mail Portal list data
conversion_surface.affected_constraint: Voting access and state election administration timing through ballot-mail distribution
conversion_surface.harm_before_review_pathway: Nonmatching or noncompliant outbound ballot mail is returned before acceptance and must be corrected before remailing
